rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding measure left Arabia no excuse that God’s religion had not been fully explained to it.
rows.anchor: of verse 24 of Sūrah Ḥā Mīm al-Sajdah this measure left the people of Arabia with no excuse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm al-Qurā means Makkah, Arabia’s central city.
rows.anchor: refer to Makkah because they imply the central city, and it was Makkah which occupied this status in Arabia.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the central city makes the communication conclusive for the country as a whole; a call from elsewhere might invite objections about addressing masses rather than its leaders and intelligentsia.
rows.anchor: If a message has been delivered to the central city, then this means that people of the country have been openly communicated it.

rows.speaker: Some people
rows.claim: Some interpreters take “those around it” to mean the whole world because Muhammad was sent to all humanity.
rows.anchor: Some people interpret the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Muhammad’s universal mission is true, reading “those around it” as the whole world exceeds the phrase’s scope and is unnecessary to the argument.
rows.anchor: clearly exceeds their ambit of application in the first place, and in the second it is not even needed for the real purpose.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad’s specific preaching sphere was Makkah and Arabia, where he directly and conclusively conveyed the truth; his general sphere was the whole world.
rows.anchor: His specific sphere relates to Makkah and Arabia and to them he conclusively communicated the truth in a direct manner

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an and Prophet charged the Muslim community with bearing witness to the true religion worldwide until the Day of Judgement.
rows.anchor: has imposed the responsibility of bearing witness to the true religion on the Muslim ummah till the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As witnesses, Muslims must testify to others as God’s messenger testified to them; one group will remain faithful even amid pervasive sin.
rows.anchor: one group among it will always adhere to the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the general warning, the Prophet is specifically to warn people about the Day of Gathering, the Day of Judgement.
rows.anchor: mention specific warning ( indhār-i khās ): the Prophet (sws) should specifically warn these people of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi identifies the term Yawm al-Jamʿ as the Day of Gathering in the warning.
rows.anchor: the day of gathering). Obviously the words

rows.speaker: unnamed objectors
rows.claim: They object that if God gave people one religion, why did He not will that everyone follow it, instead of allowing differences that end with one group in Paradise and another in Hell?
rows.anchor: This verse answers an objection

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have made everyone one community, but chose not to compel acceptance; He gave people intellect and freedom to choose His guidance and thereby become worthy of mercy.
rows.anchor: He desired that He give people vision and intellect and also give them the liberty to choose

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s will to admit people to mercy operates under His justice, which determines who enters that mercy.
rows.anchor: His justice will govern which people will enter His mercy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unjust have neither alleged deities nor any faction to accomplish or help them, so their exclusion from mercy is just and no one can alter God’s intention.
rows.anchor: only those people will be deprived of God’s mercy who are unjust to their souls and who are idolaters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and guidance depend on God’s will, which grants the impulse to believe to those who use their intellect; those who do not use it are obscured by filth from seeing guidance.
rows.anchor: His intention blesses those people the urge to accept faith who use their intellect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have forced every soul to believe, but instead tests people by allowing them to choose belief or disbelief, with Paradise or Hell as the respective outcome.
rows.anchor: if the Almighty intended to force people to accept faith, He would have made everyone a believer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a reminder, not something to force on people; the Prophet and companions should remind them, while each person may choose belief or disbelief.
rows.anchor: it is merely a reminder; so they should remind people through it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s and companions’ desire that people believe cannot succeed unless God wills it, and God’s will is governed by knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: merely having a desire can bear no fruit unless God intends and God’s intention is governed by His knowledge and His wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God admits to mercy those who do not wrong themselves, use their God-given abilities, and heed guidance; those spiritually blind will face grievous punishment.
rows.anchor: only those who do not wrong their souls and in fact make use of the abilities given to them by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about taking protectors besides God expresses wonder and negation: only God is the true protector, who raises the dead and to whom all return, so no other protector can avail anyone.
rows.anchor: Only God is the real accomplisher – both in the Herein and in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 10 carries out verse 8’s instruction to leave opponents’ disputes to God: the Prophet has delivered the truth, trusts his Lord, and asks Him to judge whether he fulfilled his duty or they failed to recognize truth.
rows.anchor: the words of this verse from the tongue of the Prophet (sws) are directed at his opponents

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person should cultivate patience, since those without it cannot carry on in this course.
rows.anchor: those who are devoid of it will not be able to proceed in this regard. Thus a person should inculcate the spirit of patience in himself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This quality is a mark of nobility and loftiness; those who acquire it are noble and lofty.
rows.anchor: this is the character of nobility and loftiness. Those who imbibe it in themselves are noble and lofty people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These directions addressed Muslims facing Quraysh before migration, political organization, and conclusive communication; afterward the Muslim polity was told to sever relations and continue fighting until Quraysh submitted to Islam’s authority.
rows.anchor: After migration, when Muslims became an organized polity and the truth was also conclusively conveyed to the Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 44–50 resume verse 36’s contrast between the opponents’ temporary worldly life and the believers’ lasting Hereafter reward; the believers’ traits make the glad tidings immediate for oppressed Muslims and foreshadow their success.
rows.anchor: The succeeding verses relate to the subject raised in verse 36. The discourse in that verse had reached the stage that the life

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse resumes by assuring the Prophet that opponents subject to God’s law cannot be guided by anyone else and will realize this too late, then gives them a final chance to reform and explains their arrogance as ingratitude for God’s favors.
rows.anchor: the earlier discourse is taken up again and first the Prophet (sws) is assured that those who are now facing the law of God cannot be guided by anyone else

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents’ arrogance comes from forgetting that everything they receive is God’s grace; they use His favors to rebel against Him.
rows.anchor: whatever a person receives, he receives with the grace of God; but man is ungrateful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s established practice leaves those who prefer straying without the will or impulse for guidance, reassuring the Prophet that he cannot guide them by his own efforts.
rows.anchor: those who are led astray by God because they prefer going astray are deprived by God from the urge and will to be guided

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The label wrongdoers shows that they deserved to be led astray: they neglected God-given capacities and innate guidance, followed desires blindly, and thereby fell into disbelief and polytheism and wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: these people in fact deserved this treatment: they deserved to be led astray because they did not use the abilities bestowed to them by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though proud now, the wrongdoers will wish after seeing punishment to return to earthly life, do good deeds, and escape it.
rows.anchor: when they see the punishment of God they will longingly express if any option remains to return to the previous world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun referring to punishment has Hell or Hellfire as its antecedent, since those are feminine nouns in Arabic; this is a common Arabic construction.
rows.anchor: is referred to by a feminine pronoun even though it is masculine because it actually refers to Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who mock punishment now will face it with heads bowed and furtive glances; Islahi compares their fear to a criminal being led to execution.
rows.anchor: When a criminal is taken to the place of his execution, he does not have the guts to open his eyes wide

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true losers are those who ruin themselves and their families or associates on Judgement Day by pressuring them or teaching them evil; worldly success is not the real measure of success.
rows.anchor: those people who not only put themselves to loss on the Day of Judgement but also their family and associates

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ warning that real failure is on Judgement Day is explained by the punishment awaiting wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: they should beware that the reason for this is that the wrongdoers will be

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Against God” means that the deities and helpers on whom the wrongdoers relied cannot protect them from God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: when on the Day of Judgement, these people will be engulfed by the punishment of God, none of their deities and helpers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 46 restates verse 44 with slightly different words: those God leaves astray because of their evil deeds have no way in this world or the next.
rows.anchor: the same subject which was discussed in verse 44 above is raised again with slight change in words.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islahi’s syntactic reading, “from God” connects to “arrives,” and “that cannot be put off” qualifies “day.”
rows.anchor: is an adjective that qualifies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns people that there is still time to answer their Lord, but when the certain Day arrives there will be no refuge or ability to reject what comes; they must submit.
rows.anchor: when the Day which is certain to come from their Lord arrives, it will be immaterial whether they accept the call or not

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word nakīr is better understood as rejecting something repulsive from a sense of honour, rather than as simple denial.
rows.anchor: However, its correct meaning is “to reject something repulsive because of a sense of honour.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not worry if people refuse: he was not sent to compel acceptance but only to deliver the message, a subject already raised in verse 6.
rows.anchor: his only responsibility is to present his message before people. In verse 6 earlier, this subject has been raised.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People evade the message because they are ungrateful: blessings make them conceited, while calamities brought by their own deeds drive them to despair and further ingratitude; their wealth has intoxicated them, though even slight torment would dishearten them.
rows.anchor: When such people receive the blessings and favours of God instead showing gratitude, they are overcome by conceit and arrogance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief that God owns the heavens and earth and alone controls creation and provision would produce gratitude for blessings and patience in trials.
rows.anchor: If these people believe that the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth belongs to God; He alone creates what He wants and bestows whatever He wants

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offspring examples specify God’s general creative power: He may give daughters, sons, both, or no children, acting with knowledge and power; people should trust Him rather than be arrogant, helpless, or serve others.
rows.anchor: mention the specific after the general: it is God Who gives daughters to whomsoever He pleases and sons to whosoever He pleases

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah’s ending echoes its opening: both present the Qur’an as revelation of the kind sent to earlier prophets, showing that the sūrah is one coherent unit.
rows.anchor: They are very similar to the words found at the beginning. This is a very clear argument on the fact that the whole sūrah from the beginning to the end is one unit.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing passage answers the preceding section’s opponents, who objected that if Muhammad receives revelation, God should speak to them too; Islahi says the answer is comprehensive and conclusive.
rows.anchor: why does not God talk to them as well?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders of polytheism fabricate religion, blindly defend it, arrogantly ignore revelation, mock what might affect hearts, and will find neither ill-gotten wealth nor invented deities able to save them from doom.
rows.anchor: The ringleaders of the creed of polytheism who have fabricated a false religion and have become so ardent in blindly supporting it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 12–15 offer a new style of arguments for monotheism and urge Muslims to remain patient and steady, ignoring idolaters; refusal harms only the rejecters.
rows.anchor: Some arguments in support of monotheism are presented in a new style and Muslims are urged to show patience and perseverance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel received political power, prophethood, ample sustenance, and leadership but failed its obligations, splitting religion from jealousy; Muslims now hold the entrusted sharīʿah and should adhere firmly, avoid Israel’s path, and not fear the Jewish–idolater alliance.
rows.anchor: they were blessed with political authority, prophethood, abundant resources of sustenance as well as the leadership of other nations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 21–37 answer rejecters’ objections to the Hereafter, depict their condition there, and return to the theme of monotheism at the end.
rows.anchor: Some objections raised by the rejecters of the Hereafter are dispelled. The state of affairs on that day of the deniers of the Hereafter is depicted.
